analysis:
The change set is documentation-only (docs/architecture/inference.md): it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds prose about tensor-parallel selection finiteness checks, a load-agreement token (qwen-tensor-parallel-selection-nonfinite-in-sum-v1), and a per-rank decode-route census log line. The supplied units are BASE excerpts (lines 838-1644) that sit outside the changed ranges (base only 3 and 5105; head 5094-5157). So I could not see the added lines directly, and the patch excerpt is truncated at the census paragraph.

The base text I examined covers Nemotron Super and GLM5Next serving and the engine mechanism. It touches the TB-007 inference engine and T-041 (prefix-cache). It states the encrypted SSD checkpoint store, the cache scope authenticated by the coordinator, and that reuse never crosses a cache scope. These statements are consistent with T-041 and make no weakening claim, for example about TTL, scope or HMAC naming.

Security-relevant observations from the patch excerpt:
- The new text describes fail-closed behavior on non-finite logits on either rank, which is an availability and integrity improvement.
- The new 'decode census' log line is per rank and per loaded model. It is described as logging projection routes, which look like model and execution metadata, not prompt content. The excerpt is truncated, so I could not confirm that nothing prompt-derived is logged. This is a remaining question for any code-side review, not a finding.

No code, config, or threat-model-relevant control changed in the visible evidence, so there is no concrete regression. The remaining uncertainty is limited to the truncated added doc content and whether the actual code matches the doc claims; the code is not supplied.
